sources.entry: Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation authoring

summary.title: Diátaxis
summary.one_liner: Diátaxis is a systematic framework that splits technical documentation into four needs and forms: tutorials, how-to guides, technical reference, and explanation.
takeaways: Documentation serves four distinct user needs, each with its own form: tutorials, how-to guides, technical reference, and explanation.
The framework addresses what to write (content), how to write it (style), and how to organise it (architecture).
Diátaxis is described as lightweight, easy to grasp, and not imposing implementation constraints.
It offers maintainers an active principle of quality to guide their work.
The site says the best way to start is applying it after reading a brief primer.
summary.summary: The Diátaxis home page presents a framework for thinking about and creating technical documentation. It identifies four user needs and matching documentation forms (tutorials, how-to guides, technical reference, and explanation) and proposes organising documentation around those structures. The page states that the approach addresses content, style, and architecture, and that it is light-weight and useful to both readers and maintainers. It also includes testimonials from organisations such as Vonage, Gatsby, and Cloudflare, which are not summarised here.
